responsibility.value: Owns the full authentication lifecycle — login, registration, logout, and password reset — bridging ASP.NET Core Identity to the application's JWT/token-revocation model.

Owns: Login flow: username lookup, active-account check, password verification with lockout, single-role invariant check, token issuance
Registration flow: delegates account creation to IUserProvisioningService, then re-issues a token for the new user
Logout: forwards jti + expiry to ITokenRevocationService so the token can no longer be used
User-enumeration protection on ForgotPasswordAsync — same response whether or not the email exists
Password reset via ASP.NET Identity's UserManager.ResetPasswordAsync
doesNotOwn: Token generation mechanics — delegated to ITokenService
New-user account creation details — delegated to IUserProvisioningService

collaborators.detail: Issues the JWT after successful login/register
LogoutAsync forwards jti + expiresAt for revocation

contracts: LoginAsync requires the user to have exactly one role assigned — this is verified explicitly, not merely assumed by the token's single-role claim shape.
ForgotPasswordAsync returns the same success message regardless of whether the email corresponds to a real account, to prevent user enumeration.
In non-development environments, the raw reset token is never logged.
assumptions: Exactly one role per user is a business invariant enforced at login time — if a user somehow has zero or multiple roles, login fails or behaves ambiguously rather than picking one.
IWebHostEnvironment correctly reports Development so the token-prefix debug log never fires outside local dev.
SignInManager's CheckPasswordSignInAsync lockout behavior (attempt counting, lockout duration) is configured correctly elsewhere in Identity setup — this class doesn't configure it.
failureModes: Login failure — invalid credentials, inactive account, or account lockout (surfaced via SignInManager's lockout support)
Login failure — user has other than exactly one role (ambiguous/misconfigured account)
Password reset — invalid/expired token rejected by UserManager.ResetPasswordAsync
architecturalNotes: The first 8 characters of the reset token are logged only in the Development environment — a deliberate debug aid, gated correctly, but worth confirming environment detection can't be spoofed in any deployment.

RegisterAsync re-looks-up the user by username after provisioning rather than receiving the created user directly from IUserProvisioningService — an extra round trip, presumably to keep the provisioning service decoupled from token issuance.
